#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: Wave 19-E (#737) — cycle with BOTH exit_when AND abort_when
# converges cleanly when exit_when matches and abort_when does NOT.
#
# Bug: dogfood 20260607140638-60666 (issue 12) — pipeline reported
# pipeline.abort despite review.verdict=approve. Wave 19-D-1 instrumentation
# pinpointed it: _cycle_check_abort_when returns 1 when its predicate does
# NOT match (the GOOD case — verdict=approve, not block). The call site
# in cycle_orchestrator_run's iter-end logic was a bare command under a
# potentially-active errexit state, where the symmetric exit_when call
# used a set +e/set -e dance to defend against it. Bash errexit kills
# cycle_orchestrator_run before reaching the cycle.iteration.complete and
# cycle.complete emits.
#
# 5-line copy-paste oversight from Wave 17-B (ADR-027, #703) adding
# abort_when. Synthetic tests didn't repro because none defined abort_when
# in their templates; the trigger was a cycle with BOTH exit_when AND
# abort_when (the retired standard.yaml's build_review_cycle; #979). This test
# locks the fix with a self-contained fixture carrying both predicates.
#
# This is the failing-test-first TDD regression lock.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
print_test_header "cycle abort_when non-match converges (Wave 19-E #737)"
setup_test_env "cycle-abort-when-no-match-converges"

export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"

STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "${STATE_FILE}.bak" "${STATE_FILE}.lock"
jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

# Standard.yaml-shape template — single cycle with BOTH exit_when AND
# abort_when defined. Exit_when looks for review=approve; abort_when looks
# for review=block. Mock dispatch returns review=approve. The cycle MUST
# converge via exit_when even though abort_when is defined-but-not-matching.
TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/abort-when-defined.yaml"
cat > "$TPL" <<'EOF'
id: abort_when_defined
name: Cycle with abort_when defined but not matching
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - the_cycle

the_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - review
  exit_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: approve
  abort_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: block
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: continue

review:
  roles: [reviewer]
EOF

# Mock dispatch — review returns approve (which exit_when matches; abort_when
# does NOT match). On caller-restored set -e, the bare abort_when check
# returns 1 (no match) and crashes the orchestrator pre-fix.
cycle_dispatch_stage() {
    local stage="$1"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"        # classified
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="approve" # raw — what abort_when/exit_when compare
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
    return 0
}

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
_TPL_STAGES=(); _TPL_CYCLES=()
load_template "$TPL" || assert_fail "template load"

# Exercise the exact errexit context the runner uses. The orchestrator
# runs with set +e internally but the caller (runner) typically has set -e
# active. Set -e here to mirror that, then call.
# Mirror runner.sh's set -e context. Capture rc via `|| rc=$?` so the
# test itself doesn't crash on any errexit-driven exit from inside the
# orchestrator; matches how runner.sh calls into the orchestrator.
set -e
rc=0
cycle_orchestrator_run "the_cycle" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE" || rc=$?

print_test_section "outer cycle converges via exit_when when abort_when is defined-but-not-matching"

# T1: cycle returns rc=0 (converged). PRE-FIX, the bare abort_when call
# under set -e crashes the function before _CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON
# is set; observed symptom: pipeline.abort fires from EXIT trap.
assert_eq "T1: cycle_orchestrator_run returns rc=0 (exit_when match=true)" "0" "$rc"

# T2: cycle.iteration.complete fired. The bug skips this emit when abort_when
# crashes the orchestrator.
iter_complete=$(jq -c 'select(.type=="cycle.iteration.complete" and .data.cycle_id=="the_cycle")' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
assert_eq "T2: cycle.iteration.complete fired (the bug skips this)" "1" "$iter_complete"

# T3: cycle.complete fired with reason=converged.
cycle_complete=$(jq -c 'select(.type=="cycle.complete" and .data.cycle_id=="the_cycle")' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
assert_eq "T3: cycle.complete fired" "1" "$cycle_complete"

cycle_reason=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="cycle.complete" and .data.cycle_id=="the_cycle") | .data.reason' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
assert_eq "T4: cycle.complete reason=converged (NOT aborted)" "converged" "$cycle_reason"

# T5: Wave 19-C-1 predicate event for abort_when fired (proves the function
# RAN — it emitted its event then returned 1).
abort_pred=$(jq -c 'select(.type=="cycle.predicate.evaluated" and .data.kind=="abort_when" and .data.cycle_id=="the_cycle")' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
assert_eq "T5: cycle.predicate.evaluated kind=abort_when fired (predicate function ran)" "1" "$abort_pred"

abort_match=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="cycle.predicate.evaluated" and .data.kind=="abort_when") | .data.match' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
assert_eq "T6: abort_when match=false (verdict=approve, not block)" "false" "$abort_match"

# T7: terminated_reason global reflects converged.
assert_eq "T7: _CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON=converged" "converged" "${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-MISSING}"

# T8: exit_when predicate also fired and matched.
exit_pred_match=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="cycle.predicate.evaluated" and .data.kind=="exit_when") | .data.match' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
assert_eq "T8: exit_when match=true (predicate evaluated before abort_when crash)" "true" "$exit_pred_match"

print_test_section "nested-cycle production scenario (mirror dogfood 20260607140638-60666)"

: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "${STATE_FILE}.bak" "${STATE_FILE}.lock"
jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

# Classic outer-remediation shape: outer build_review_cycle = [build_test_cycle, review]
# (the retired standard.yaml once shipped this; #979 — fixture is self-contained)
# with BOTH exit_when AND abort_when. Inner build_test_cycle converges, then
# review approves. Outer should converge via exit_when on review.verdict=approve.
TPL_NESTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/nested-prod.yaml"
cat > "$TPL_NESTED" <<'EOF'
id: nested_prod
name: Nested cycle with abort_when (production shape)
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - build_review_cycle

build_review_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - build_test_cycle
    - review
  exit_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: approve
  abort_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: block
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: continue

build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - build
    - test
  exit_when:
    stage: test
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue

build:
  roles: [builder]

test:
  roles: [tester]

review:
  roles: [reviewer]
EOF

cycle_dispatch_stage() {
    local stage="$1"
    case "$stage" in
        build|test)
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="pass"
            ;;
        review)
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="approve"
            ;;
    esac
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
    return 0
}

_TPL_STAGES=(); _TPL_CYCLES=()
load_template "$TPL_NESTED" || assert_fail "nested template load"

set -e
rc=0
cycle_orchestrator_run "build_review_cycle" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE" || rc=$?

# T11: nested-outer cycle returns rc=0.
assert_eq "T11: nested build_review_cycle returns rc=0" "0" "$rc"

# T12: outer build_review_cycle's iteration.complete fired (the dogfood-missing event).
nested_iter_complete=$(jq -c 'select(.type=="cycle.iteration.complete" and .data.cycle_id=="build_review_cycle")' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
assert_eq "T12: nested build_review_cycle's cycle.iteration.complete fired (dogfood-missing event)" "1" "$nested_iter_complete"

# T13: outer build_review_cycle's cycle.complete fired with reason=converged.
nested_complete=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="cycle.complete" and .data.cycle_id=="build_review_cycle") | .data.reason' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
assert_eq "T13: nested build_review_cycle cycle.complete reason=converged" "converged" "$nested_complete"

# T14: outer's abort_when predicate fired (proves _cycle_check_abort_when ran).
nested_abort_pred=$(jq -c 'select(.type=="cycle.predicate.evaluated" and .data.cycle_id=="build_review_cycle" and .data.kind=="abort_when")' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
assert_eq "T14: outer's abort_when predicate event fired" "1" "$nested_abort_pred"

print_test_section "regression guard: cycle without abort_when (unchanged path) still works"

: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "${STATE_FILE}.bak" "${STATE_FILE}.lock"
jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

TPL2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/no-abort-when.yaml"
cat > "$TPL2" <<'EOF'
id: no_abort_when
name: Cycle without abort_when (regression guard)
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - the_cycle

the_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - review
  exit_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: approve
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: continue

review:
  roles: [reviewer]
EOF

_TPL_STAGES=(); _TPL_CYCLES=()
load_template "$TPL2" || assert_fail "no-abort-when template load"

# Mirror runner.sh's set -e context. Capture rc via `|| rc=$?` so the
# test itself doesn't crash on any errexit-driven exit from inside the
# orchestrator; matches how runner.sh calls into the orchestrator.
set -e
rc=0
cycle_orchestrator_run "the_cycle" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE" || rc=$?

assert_eq "T9: regression guard — no-abort_when cycle converges rc=0" "0" "$rc"

reg_cycle_complete=$(jq -c 'select(.type=="cycle.complete" and .data.cycle_id=="the_cycle")' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
assert_eq "T10: regression guard — cycle.complete emitted" "1" "$reg_cycle_complete"

print_test_section "SPEC-4 — full eight-op set in single-condition _cycle_check_until"
# Tests FAIL before #1760 because neq/gt/gte/lt/lte/contains/matches are absent
# from the evaluator (old code has 'ne' and 'eq' only).
# Set internal state directly (same approach as cycle-multi-exit-when-test.sh).

_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR=""   # single-condition mode

# eq — sanity / regression
_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE="s1"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD="verdict"
_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP="eq"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="pass"
blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-4] eq: match → rc=0" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"fail","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-4] eq: no-match → rc=1" "1" "$rc"

# neq (was 'ne' in old code — must be renamed to neq)
_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP="neq"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="fail"
blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-4] neq: verdict!=fail → rc=0" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"fail","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-4] neq: verdict==fail → rc=1" "1" "$rc"

# gt
_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD="score"
_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP="gt"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="5"
blob='{"s1":{"score":"10","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-4] gt: 10>5 → rc=0" "0" "$rc"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Tests: ADR-027 recursive-flow loader — new-shape template parsing (Wave 17-B, #703)
3	#
4	# Asserts the new top-level `flow:` + stage-section shape loads correctly:
5	#   - reserved metadata (id, name, defaults) extracted
6	#   - top-level flow list captured
7	#   - leaf stage sections parsed into _TPL_STAGE_* per-id vars
8	#   - cycle stage section parsed into _TPL_CYCLE_* + _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id>=cycle
9	#   - exit_when / abort_when (optional) parsed
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
13	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
14	
15	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
16	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
17	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
18	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
19	
20	print_test_header "template loader — ADR-027 recursive flow (Wave 17-B)"
21	setup_test_env "template-loader-recursive-flow"
22	
23	# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
24	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
25	
26	NEW_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/new-shape.yaml"
27	cat > "$NEW_TPL" <<'EOF'
28	id: new-shape
29	name: New Shape Pipeline
30	extends: null
31	defaults:
32	  strategy: fanout
33	
34	flow:
35	  - intake
36	  - plan
37	  - build_test_cycle
38	  - review
39	
40	intake:
41	  gate: auto
42	  roles: [intake]
43	  io:
44	    destinations: [file, stdout]
45	    tail_lines: 200
46	
47	plan:
48	  gate: auto
49	  roles: [planner]
50	  io:
51	    destinations: [file, stdout]
52	    tail_lines: 200
53	  router:
54	    timeout_s: 300
55	    max_turns: 25
56	
57	build_test_cycle:
58	  type: cycle
59	  flow:
60	    - build
61	    - test
62	    - test_assessment
63	  exit_when:
64	    stage: test_assessment
65	    field: verdict
66	    op: eq
67	    value: pass
68	  max_iterations: 3
69	  on_max: continue
70	
71	build:
72	  gate: auto
73	  roles: [builder]
74	  io:
75	    destinations: [file, stdout]
76	    tail_lines: 200
77	  router:
78	    timeout_s: 900
79	
80	test:
81	  gate: auto
82	  roles: [tester]
83	  io:
84	    destinations: [file, stdout]
85	    tail_lines: 200
86	
87	test_assessment:
88	  gate: auto
89	  roles: [test_assessment]

92	    tail_lines: 200

95	    max_turns: 25
96	
97	review:
98	  gate: auto
99	  roles: [reviewer]
100	  io:
101	    destinations: [file, stdout]
102	    tail_lines: 200
103	  router:
104	    timeout_s: 300
105	    max_turns: 25
106	EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: ADR-027 recursive-flow loader — new-shape template parsing (Wave 17-B, #703)
#
# Asserts the new top-level `flow:` + stage-section shape loads correctly:
#   - reserved metadata (id, name, defaults) extracted
#   - top-level flow list captured
#   - leaf stage sections parsed into _TPL_STAGE_* per-id vars
#   - cycle stage section parsed into _TPL_CYCLE_* + _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id>=cycle
#   - exit_when / abort_when (optional) parsed
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "template loader — ADR-027 recursive flow (Wave 17-B)"
setup_test_env "template-loader-recursive-flow"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

NEW_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/new-shape.yaml"
cat > "$NEW_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: new-shape
name: New Shape Pipeline
extends: null
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - intake
  - plan
  - build_test_cycle
  - review

intake:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

plan:
  gate: auto
  roles: [planner]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

build_test_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - build
    - test
    - test_assessment
  exit_when:
    stage: test_assessment
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 3
  on_max: continue

build:
  gate: auto
  roles: [builder]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 900

test:
  gate: auto
  roles: [tester]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200

test_assessment:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_assessment]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25

review:
  gate: auto
  roles: [reviewer]
  io:
    destinations: [file, stdout]
    tail_lines: 200
  router:
    timeout_s: 300
    max_turns: 25
EOF

# Clear any module-level state from a previous test in the same shell.
_TPL_STAGES=()
_TPL_CYCLES=()
_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS=()

# T1: load_template succeeds on new shape.
set +e
load_template "$NEW_TPL"; rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "T1: load_template new shape rc=0" "0" "$rc"

# T2: top-level flow captured as _TPL_STAGES (flattened).
# Expected flat list: intake plan build test test_assessment review
joined="${_TPL_STAGES[*]}"
assert_eq "T2: _TPL_STAGES expanded flat from new flow" \
    "intake plan build test test_assessment review" "$joined"

# T3: defaults.strategy preserved.
assert_eq "T3: defaults.strategy=fanout" "fanout" "$_TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY"

# T4: cycle id captured.
assert_eq "T4: _TPL_CYCLES contains build_test_cycle" \
    "build_test_cycle" "${_TPL_CYCLES[*]}"

# T5: stage type discriminators set.
assert_eq "T5: build_test_cycle type=cycle" "cycle" \
    "${_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_build_test_cycle:-}"
assert_eq "T5: intake type=leaf" "leaf" "${_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_intake:-}"
assert_eq "T5: review type=leaf" "leaf" "${_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_review:-}"

# T6: cycle's exit_when fields exported in the same shape the orchestrator
# reads today (_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_* — back-compat with existing reader).
assert_eq "T6: until stage=test_assessment" "test_assessment" \
    "${_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_build_test_cycle:-}"
assert_eq "T6: until field=verdict" "verdict" \
    "${_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_build_test_cycle:-}"
assert_eq "T6: until op=eq" "eq" "${_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_build_test_cycle:-}"
assert_eq "T6: until value=pass" "pass" \
    "${_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_build_test_cycle:-}"

# T7: cycle's flow members captured.
assert_eq "T7: cycle stages csv" "build,test,test_assessment" \
    "${_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_build_test_cycle:-}"

# T8: (retired) cycle `feedback:` wires — load_template refuses them
# (ADR-055 §4, amended 2026-10-12; core-pipeline-template-cycles-test.sh T3).

# T9: per-stage attrs parsed for cycle members (build/test/test_assessment).
assert_eq "T9: build roles" "builder" "${_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_build:-}"
assert_eq "T9: test roles" "tester" "${_TPL_STAGE_ROLES_test:-}"
assert_eq "T9: build router.timeout_s=900" "900" \
    "${_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_build:-}"

# T10: per-stage io for leaf stage.
assert_eq "T10: intake io dests" "file,stdout" \
    "${_TPL_STAGE_IO_DESTS_intake:-}"

# T11 (Copilot P2): inline-list `flow: [a, b]` form is detected as new shape
# and parses correctly (mirrors what the cycle `flow:` already supports).
INLINE_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/inline-flow.yaml"
cat > "$INLINE_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: inline
flow: [intake, plan, review]

intake:
  roles: [intake]

plan:
  roles: [planner]

review:
  roles: [reviewer]
EOF
_TPL_STAGES=()
_TPL_CYCLES=()
set +e
load_template "$INLINE_TPL"; rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "T11: inline flow form loads rc=0" "0" "$rc"
assert_eq "T11: stages from inline flow" "intake plan review" "${_TPL_STAGES[*]}"

# ── [#1760/SPEC-1] abort_when.op outside the eight-op set refused at load ──────
# load_template must return non-zero and emit an error naming the loop ID,
# the field, the bad op, and the valid set. Tests FAIL before #1760 (no
# abort_when op validation in _tpl_validate_cycles).

BAD_AW_OP_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bad-abort-op.yaml"
cat > "$BAD_AW_OP_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: bad-abort-op
name: Bad abort_when op test
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - the_cycle

the_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - review
  exit_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  abort_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: contains_all
    value: block
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: continue

review:
  roles: [reviewer]
EOF

_TPL_STAGES=(); _TPL_CYCLES=()
set +e
bad_aw_err=$(load_template "$BAD_AW_OP_TPL" 2>&1); bad_aw_rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-1] abort_when bad op refused (rc!=0)" "1" "$bad_aw_rc"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-1] error names the loop" "$bad_aw_err" "the_cycle"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-1] error names the field" "$bad_aw_err" "verdict"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-1] error names the bad op" "$bad_aw_err" "contains_all"
# The valid set must appear in the error. Check for ops that are NOT substrings
# of the bad op name 'contains_all' — neq, gte, lte, matches are all in the
# eight-op set but none appear as a substring of 'contains_all'. Checking only
# 'contains' would pass trivially because 'contains_all' contains 'contains'.
if grep -qE 'neq|gte|lte|matches' <<< "$bad_aw_err" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-1] error names the valid op set"
else
    assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-1] error names the valid op set" \
        "expected a valid-set member distinct from 'contains_all' (neq/gte/lte/matches) in: $bad_aw_err"
fi

# ── [#1760/SPEC-2] single-condition until.op outside eight-op set refused ──────
# The single-condition exit_when op must also be validated at load time.
# Tests FAIL before #1760 (single-condition until.op has no validation).

BAD_UNTIL_OP_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bad-until-op.yaml"
cat > "$BAD_UNTIL_OP_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: bad-until-op
name: Bad single-condition exit_when op
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - the_cycle

the_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - review
  exit_when:
    stage: review
    field: verdict
    op: in
    value: pass
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: continue

review:
  roles: [reviewer]
EOF

_TPL_STAGES=(); _TPL_CYCLES=()
set +e
bad_until_err=$(load_template "$BAD_UNTIL_OP_TPL" 2>&1); bad_until_rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-2] single-condition bad op refused (rc!=0)" "1" "$bad_until_rc"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-2] error names the loop" "$bad_until_err" "the_cycle"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-2] error names the bad op" "$bad_until_err" "in"

# ── [#1760/SPEC-3] multi-condition exit_when op outside eight-op set refused ──
# Each condition's op in a multi-condition exit_when must be validated.
# Old code validates only eq|ne|in; tests FAIL before #1760 (ne is rejected
# post-fix since it is not in the eight-op set).

BAD_MULTI_OP_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bad-multi-op.yaml"
cat > "$BAD_MULTI_OP_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: bad-multi-op
name: Bad multi-condition exit_when op
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - the_cycle

the_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - gate_a
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: gate_a, field: verdict, op: ne, value: fail }
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: continue

gate_a:
  roles: [checker]
EOF

_TPL_STAGES=(); _TPL_CYCLES=()
set +e
bad_multi_err=$(load_template "$BAD_MULTI_OP_TPL" 2>&1); bad_multi_rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-3] multi-condition bad op refused (rc!=0)" "1" "$bad_multi_rc"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-3] error names the loop" "$bad_multi_err" "the_cycle"
assert_contains "[#1760/SPEC-3] error names the bad op" "$bad_multi_err" "ne"

# ── [#1760/SPEC-9] ADR-027 has ## Enforced by section; removed from baseline ──
# Post-fix, ADR-027 gains its "## Enforced by" section naming the test files
# that enforce the eight-op set.  The baseline entry is removed at the same time.
# This test does not need to fail before the change (no-code SPEC).

ADR027="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-027-recursive-flow-template-format.md"
if grep -q '## Enforced by' "$ADR027" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-9] ADR-027 has ## Enforced by section"
else
    assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-9] ADR-027 has ## Enforced by section" \
        "section missing from $ADR027"
fi

# Extract the ## Enforced by section content (from its heading to the next
# level-2 heading). Then verify each of the four test files that enforce
# the eight-op set are named inside it.
_spec9_section=$(awk '/^## Enforced by/{f=1;next} f && /^## /{exit} f{print}' "$ADR027" 2>/dev/null || true)
for _spec9_file in \
    "tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh" \
    "tests/integration/cycle-abort-when-no-match-converges-test.sh" \
    "tests/integration/cycle-orchestrator-abort-when-test.sh" \
    "tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-events-test.sh"
do
    if grep -qF "$_spec9_file" <<< "$_spec9_section" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-9] ## Enforced by names $_spec9_file"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-9] ## Enforced by names $_spec9_file" \
            "not found in Enforced by section of $ADR027"
    fi
done

BASELINE="$REPO_ROOT/config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
if grep -qF 'ADR-027-recursive-flow-template-format.md' "$BASELINE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-9] ADR-027 is removed from adr-enforcement-baseline.txt" \
        "entry still present in $BASELINE"
else
    assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-9] ADR-027 is removed from adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
fi

print_test_results

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: cycle-* event registrations in config/event-schema.json (ADR-021, #512)
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
print_test_header "cycle events — schema registrations (ADR-021)"
setup_test_env "cycle-events"

SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"

# All cycle events that MUST be registered per ADR-021 §Event-schema additions
required_events=(
    "cycle.start"
    "cycle.complete"
    "cycle.plateau"
    "cycle.divergence"
    "cycle.iteration.complete"
    "cycle.aborted"
    "cycle.config.invalid"
    "cycle.iteration.verdict_missing"
    "cycle.history.lost"
    "cycle.metric.invalid"
    "cycle.plateau.skipped"
    "cycle.iter.stale_artifact"
)

for ev in "${required_events[@]}"; do
    if jq -e --arg t "$ev" '.known_types | index($t)' "$SCHEMA" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "event registered: $ev"
    else
        assert_fail "event registered: $ev" "missing from known_types"
    fi
done

# SPEC-3: the cycle.feedback.* events are retired with template feedback wires
# (ADR-055 §4, amended 2026-10-12) and are no longer registered.
for ev in cycle.feedback.missing cycle.feedback.absent; do
    if jq -e --arg t "$ev" '.known_types | index($t)' "$SCHEMA" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_fail "[SPEC-3] retired $ev is not registered" "still in known_types"
    else
        assert_pass "[SPEC-3] retired $ev is not registered"
    fi
done

print_test_section "SPEC-7 / SPEC-8 — evaluator op guards"
# Source cycle-orchestrator to get the evaluator functions.
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"

# ── [#1760/SPEC-7] gt/gte/lt/lte with non-numeric operand emits error ──────────
# Must NOT silently evaluate to false; must emit a diagnostic and return 1.
# Tests FAIL before #1760 (numeric ops not yet present in evaluators).

# Helper: call each evaluator with a non-numeric value for a numeric op,
# capture stderr, verify rc=1 AND an error message appears.

# --- _cycle_check_until (single-condition) ---
_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR=""
_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE="s1"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD="score"

for _spec7_op in gt gte lt lte; do
    _CYCLE_UNTIL_OP="$_spec7_op"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="5"
    blob='{"s1":{"score":"notanumber","status":"complete"}}'
    set +e
    _spec7_err=$(2>&1 _cycle_check_until "$blob"); _spec7_rc=$?
    set -e
    assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_until: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric → rc=1 (error, not silent false)" \
        "1" "$_spec7_rc"
    if [[ -n "$_spec7_err" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_until: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error message"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_until: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error message" \
            "no output on stderr/stdout for op=${_spec7_op} value=notanumber"
    fi
done

# --- _cycle_eval_one_condition (multi-condition) ---
# Set template vars for a single multi-condition entry using each numeric op,
# then call _cycle_load_template and _cycle_check_until (which calls _cycle_eval_one_condition).
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

for _spec7_op in gt gte lt lte; do
    _TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR_spec7_cycle="all"
    _TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COUNT_spec7_cycle="1"
    _TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_STAGE_spec7_cycle="s1"
    _TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_FIELD_spec7_cycle="score"
    _TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_OP_spec7_cycle="$_spec7_op"
    _TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_VALUE_spec7_cycle="5"
    _CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="spec7_cycle"
    _CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
    # Protected so a missing _cycle_load_template (pre-#1760) does not stop the file.
    set +e; _cycle_load_template "spec7_cycle"; _s7_mc_rc=$?; set -e
    blob='{"s1":{"score":"notanumber","status":"complete"}}'
    set +e
    _spec7_err=$(2>&1 _cycle_check_until "$blob"); _spec7_rc=$?
    set -e
    if [[ "$_s7_mc_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_eval_one_condition: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric → rc=1" \
            "_cycle_load_template failed (pre-#1760: function may not exist, rc=$_s7_mc_rc)"
        assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_eval_one_condition: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error" \
            "_cycle_load_template failed (pre-#1760: function may not exist, rc=$_s7_mc_rc)"
    else
        assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_eval_one_condition: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric → rc=1" \
            "1" "$_spec7_rc"
        if [[ -n "$_spec7_err" ]]; then
            assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_eval_one_condition: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_eval_one_condition: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error" \
                "no output for op=${_spec7_op} value=notanumber"
        fi
    fi
done

# --- _cycle_check_abort_when ---
for _spec7_op in gt gte lt lte; do
    _TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_STAGE_spec7_aw="s1"
    _TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_FIELD_spec7_aw="score"
    _TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_spec7_aw="$_spec7_op"
    _TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_spec7_aw="5"
    _TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_spec7_aw="s1"
    _TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_spec7_aw="verdict"
    _TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_spec7_aw="eq"
    _TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_spec7_aw="pass"
    _TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_spec7_aw="s1"
    _CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="spec7_aw"
    _CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
    # Protected so a missing _cycle_load_template (pre-#1760) does not stop the file.
    set +e; _cycle_load_template "spec7_aw"; _s7_aw_rc=$?; set -e
    blob='{"s1":{"score":"notanumber","status":"complete"}}'
    set +e
    _spec7_err=$(2>&1 _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"); _spec7_rc=$?
    set -e
    if [[ "$_s7_aw_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_abort_when: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric → rc=1" \
            "_cycle_load_template failed (pre-#1760: function may not exist, rc=$_s7_aw_rc)"
        assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_abort_when: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error" \
            "_cycle_load_template failed (pre-#1760: function may not exist, rc=$_s7_aw_rc)"
    else
        assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_abort_when: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric → rc=1" \
            "1" "$_spec7_rc"
        if [[ -n "$_spec7_err" ]]; then
            assert_pass "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_abort_when: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-7] _cycle_check_abort_when: ${_spec7_op} non-numeric emits error" \
                "no output for op=${_spec7_op} value=notanumber"
        fi
    fi
done

# ── [#1760/SPEC-8] *) branch returns 1 on unrecognized op ──────────────────────
# Each evaluator's *) / default branch must return 1 (not silently skip).
# Tests FAIL before #1760 (no *) branch in any evaluator).

# _cycle_check_until: unrecognized op
_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR=""
_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE="s1"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD="verdict"
_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP="bogus_op"; _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE="pass"
blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-8] _cycle_check_until: bogus_op → rc=1 (not silent skip)" "1" "$rc"

# _cycle_eval_one_condition: unrecognized op (via multi-condition mode)
_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR_spec8_cycle="all"
_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_COUNT_spec8_cycle="1"
_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_STAGE_spec8_cycle="s1"
_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_FIELD_spec8_cycle="verdict"
_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_OP_spec8_cycle="bogus_op"
_TPL_CYCLE_EXIT_1_VALUE_spec8_cycle="pass"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="spec8_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
# Protected so a missing _cycle_load_template (pre-#1760) does not stop the file.
set +e; _cycle_load_template "spec8_cycle"; _s8_mc_rc=$?; set -e
blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_until "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
if [[ "$_s8_mc_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1760/SPEC-8] _cycle_eval_one_condition: bogus_op → rc=1 (not silent skip)" \
        "_cycle_load_template failed (pre-#1760: function may not exist, rc=$_s8_mc_rc)"
else
    assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-8] _cycle_eval_one_condition: bogus_op → rc=1 (not silent skip)" "1" "$rc"
fi

# _cycle_check_abort_when: unrecognized op
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_STAGE_spec8_aw="s1"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_FIELD_spec8_aw="verdict"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_spec8_aw="bogus_op"

_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_spec8_aw="verdict"
_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_spec8_aw="eq"
_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_spec8_aw="pass"

_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="spec8_aw"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
# Protected so a missing _cycle_load_template (pre-#1760) does not stop the file.
set +e; _cycle_load_template "spec8_aw"; _s8_aw_rc=$?; set -e
blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration: ADR-027 abort_when predicate semantics (Wave 17-B, #703).
3	#
4	# abort_when (optional) is a predicate that, when matched, terminates the
5	# pipeline: the loop returns 1, ends with outcome aborted and reason
6	# cycle_abort, and records the abort word `cycle_abort` (ADR-025), which every
7	# enclosing cycle and the runner read on their way out. Distinct from a SIGINT
8	# abort (word sigint) and from blocked (outcome interrupted, no abort word).
9	#
10	# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): this used to be a new rc class, rc=6. No rc carries the
11	# reason any more — the word does.
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
15	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
16	
17	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
18	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
19	print_test_header "cycle-orchestrator — abort_when (ADR-027 / Wave 17-B)"
20	setup_test_env "cycle-orch-abortwhen"
21	
22	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
23	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
24	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
25	export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
26	
27	# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
28	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"
29	
30	STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
31	: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
32	rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "${STATE_FILE}.bak" "${STATE_FILE}.lock"
33	jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"
34	
35	ABORT_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/abort.yaml"
36	cat > "$ABORT_TPL" <<'EOF'
37	id: abort-test
38	name: abort_when test
39	defaults:
40	  strategy: fanout
41	
42	flow:
43	  - bt_cycle
44	
45	bt_cycle:
46	  type: cycle
47	  flow:
48	    - build
49	    - test
50	  exit_when:
51	    stage: test
52	    field: verdict
53	    op: eq
54	    value: pass
55	  abort_when:
56	    stage: test
57	    field: verdict
58	    op: eq
59	    value: corrupt
60	  max_iterations: 5
61	  on_max: continue
62	
63	build:
64	  roles: [builder]
65	
66	test:
67	  roles: [tester]
68	EOF
69	
70	# Mock: build always passes; test returns "corrupt" on iter 1 (trigger abort).
71	cycle_dispatch_stage() {
72	    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
73	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
74	    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
75	    case "$stage" in
76	        build) _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass" ;;
77	        test)  _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="corrupt"
78	               _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
79	               return 1
80	               ;;
81	    esac
82	    return 0
83	}
84	
85	# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
86	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
87	_TPL_STAGES=()
88	_TPL_CYCLES=()
89	set +e
90	load_template "$ABORT_TPL"; rc=$?
91	set -e
92	assert_eq "T1: template loads rc=0" "0" "$rc"
93	
94	set +e
95	cycle_orchestrator_run "bt_cycle" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
96	rc=$?
97	set -e
98	
99	# T2: rc=1 with outcome aborted — the word, not a number, says cycle_abort.
100	assert_eq "T2: orchestrator returns rc=1, outcome aborted" "1 aborted" "$rc ${_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME:-unset}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: ADR-027 abort_when predicate semantics (Wave 17-B, #703).
#
# abort_when (optional) is a predicate that, when matched, terminates the
# pipeline: the loop returns 1, ends with outcome aborted and reason
# cycle_abort, and records the abort word `cycle_abort` (ADR-025), which every
# enclosing cycle and the runner read on their way out. Distinct from a SIGINT
# abort (word sigint) and from blocked (outcome interrupted, no abort word).
#
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): this used to be a new rc class, rc=6. No rc carries the
# reason any more — the word does.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
print_test_header "cycle-orchestrator — abort_when (ADR-027 / Wave 17-B)"
setup_test_env "cycle-orch-abortwhen"

export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"; mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"

STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "${STATE_FILE}.bak" "${STATE_FILE}.lock"
jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

ABORT_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/abort.yaml"
cat > "$ABORT_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: abort-test
name: abort_when test
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - bt_cycle

bt_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - build
    - test
  exit_when:
    stage: test
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  abort_when:
    stage: test
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: corrupt
  max_iterations: 5
  on_max: continue

build:
  roles: [builder]

test:
  roles: [tester]
EOF

# Mock: build always passes; test returns "corrupt" on iter 1 (trigger abort).
cycle_dispatch_stage() {
    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
    case "$stage" in
        build) _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass" ;;
        test)  _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="corrupt"
               _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
               return 1
               ;;
    esac
    return 0
}

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
_TPL_STAGES=()
_TPL_CYCLES=()
set +e
load_template "$ABORT_TPL"; rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "T1: template loads rc=0" "0" "$rc"

set +e
cycle_orchestrator_run "bt_cycle" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
rc=$?
set -e

# T2: rc=1 with outcome aborted — the word, not a number, says cycle_abort.
assert_eq "T2: orchestrator returns rc=1, outcome aborted" "1 aborted" "$rc ${_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME:-unset}"

# T3: terminated reason set.
assert_eq "T3: reason=cycle_abort" "cycle_abort" "$_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON"

# T4: the abort is recorded as the word cycle_abort, so an enclosing
# dispatcher's post-flight check propagates the loop's rc=1 outward.
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh"
assert_eq "T4: the recorded abort word is cycle_abort" "cycle_abort" "$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"
set +e
_zbuild_propagate_abort "$rc"; rc2=$?
set -e
assert_eq "T4: _zbuild_propagate_abort on the loop's rc=1 propagates (returns 1)" "1" "$rc2"

# T5: a benign rc is never an abort (smoke check).
set +e
_zbuild_propagate_abort 0; rc3=$?
set -e
assert_eq "T5: rc=0 returns 0 (non-abort)" "0" "$rc3"

# T6 (Copilot P1): structural — the runner ends the run on the recorded abort
# WORD, and no longer branches on rc=6 (#1850). If it still read the number,
# a loop returning 1 for cycle_abort would fall through as an ordinary failed
# cycle and abort_when would silently no-op at the pipeline level. The
# behavior (cycle_abort → status interrupted, pipeline.aborted reason
# cycle_abort) is pinned by runner-cycle-rc-action-mapping-test.sh.
RUNNER_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
if grep -qE '_rc -eq 6' "$RUNNER_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "T6: runner reads the abort word, not rc=6" \
        "runner.sh still branches on rc=6: $(grep -nE '_rc -eq 6' "$RUNNER_FILE" | tr '\n' ' ')"
elif ! grep -q '_zbuild_abort_reason' "$RUNNER_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "T6: runner reads the abort word, not rc=6" \
        "runner.sh never calls _zbuild_abort_reason"
else
    assert_pass "T6: runner reads the abort word, not rc=6"
fi

print_test_section "SPEC-6 — full eight-op set in abort_when evaluator (_cycle_check_abort_when)"
# _cycle_check_abort_when: rc=0 = condition matched (DO abort), rc=1 = no match.
# Set internal abort_when state directly via _cycle_load_template after writing
# the template-level vars, so we bypass load_template op validation.
# Tests FAIL before #1760 because neq/gt/gte/lt/lte/contains/matches are absent
# from _cycle_check_abort_when.

# eq (regression)
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_STAGE_aw_cycle="s1"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_FIELD_aw_cycle="verdict"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="eq"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="block"
_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_aw_cycle="s1"
_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_aw_cycle="verdict"
_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_aw_cycle="eq"
_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_aw_cycle="pass"
_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_aw_cycle="s1"
_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_s1="leaf"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"block","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] eq: verdict==block → rc=0 (abort matched)" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"approve","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] eq: verdict==approve → rc=1 (no match)" "1" "$rc"

# neq
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="neq"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="pass"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"fail","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] neq: fail!=pass → rc=0 (abort matched)" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"verdict":"pass","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] neq: pass==pass → rc=1 (no match)" "1" "$rc"

# gt
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_FIELD_aw_cycle="score"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="gt"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="10"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"15","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] gt: 15>10 → rc=0 (abort matched)" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"5","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] gt: 5>10 → rc=1 (no match)" "1" "$rc"

# gte
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="gte"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="10"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"10","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] gte: 10>=10 → rc=0 (abort matched)" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"9","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] gte: 9>=10 → rc=1 (no match)" "1" "$rc"

# lt
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="lt"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="5"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"2","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] lt: 2<5 → rc=0 (abort matched)" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"8","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] lt: 8<5 → rc=1 (no match)" "1" "$rc"

# lte
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="lte"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="5"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"5","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] lte: 5<=5 → rc=0 (abort matched)" "0" "$rc"

blob='{"s1":{"score":"6","status":"complete"}}'
set +e; _cycle_check_abort_when "$blob"; rc=$?; set -e
assert_eq "[#1760/SPEC-6] lte: 6<=5 → rc=1 (no match)" "1" "$rc"

# contains
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_FIELD_aw_cycle="reason"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_aw_cycle="contains"
_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_aw_cycle="corrupt"
_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID="aw_cycle"
_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER=1
_cycle_load_template "aw_cycle"

121	# ─── Master trap — kills children, calls hook, removes auto temp dir ─────────
122	# _HARNESS_SIGNAL: set by dedicated INT/TERM wrappers before calling cleanup,
123	# so _test_harness_cleanup can re-raise and exit 128+signal instead of
124	# returning into the interrupted test body (which would produce bogus failures).
125	# _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP: idempotency guard — prevents double cleanup when both
126	# a signal handler and the EXIT trap would otherwise call the body.
127	_HARNESS_SIGNAL=""
128	_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=0

130	_test_harness_cleanup() {
131	    [[ "${_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
132	    _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=1
133	    _kill_test_children
134	    _test_cleanup_hook
135	    if [[ -n "${AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -d "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
136	        rm -rf "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
137	    fi
138	    # Wave 19-L (#749): rm each named TEST_TEMP_DIR setup_test_env created
139	    # so tests that forgot _test_cleanup_hook / cleanup_test_env stop
140	    # leaking. Path-prefix guard against accidental rm-rf-/: each tracked
141	    # path must live under the source-time tmp-root captured in
142	    # _ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT. Using the CURRENT $TMPDIR would fail when tests
143	    # re-export TMPDIR (Copilot review #751); the source-time root is
144	    # stable for the process lifetime since AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR was created
145	    # there. (mktemp -d always returns an absolute path so the prefix
146	    # check is meaningful.)
147	    local _trk
148	    for _trk in "${_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
149	        [[ -z "$_trk" ]] && continue
150	        [[ "$_trk" == "$_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT"/* ]] || continue
151	        [[ -d "$_trk" ]] && rm -rf "$_trk" 2>/dev/null || true
152	    done
153	    # Signal-triggered teardown: clear both the signal trap and EXIT so the
154	    # re-raised signal exits with 128+N (143/130) without running EXIT again.
155	    if [[ -n "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL:-}" ]]; then
156	        trap - "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" EXIT
157	        kill -"${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" $$
158	    fi
159	}

161	# Thin wrappers installed for TERM and INT: record the in-flight signal name
162	# then call the shared cleanup body. The cleanup body re-raises at the tail
163	# so the process exits 128+signal instead of returning into the test body.
164	_harness_signal_handler() {
165	    local _sig="$1"
166	    _HARNESS_SIGNAL="$_sig"
167	    _test_harness_cleanup
168	}

179	assert_pass() {
180	    local desc="$1"
181	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
182	    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
183	    # #600: ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET=1 suppresses per-assertion echoes to keep the
184	    # pipeline test-stage banner compact. Counters still update; assert_fail
185	    # is intentionally NOT gated (failures always surface).
186	    [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
187	    echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${RESET} ${desc}"
188	}

190	assert_fail() {
191	    local desc="$1"
192	    local detail="${2:-}"
193	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
194	    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
195	    FAILURES[${#FAILURES[@]}]="$desc"
196	    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET} ${desc}"
197	    # An `if`, not `[[ … ]] && …` as the last line: with no detail that returned
198	    # 1, and under `set -e` the file stopped at its first failure — every later
199	    # assertion went unmeasured (#2234; 13 SPECs on #1835).
200	    if [[ -n "$detail" ]]; then echo -e "    ${DIM}${detail}${RESET}"; fi
201	    return 0
202	}

429	# ─── Reserved test identity (#1921 follow-up) ───────────────────────────────
430	# Tests used real issue numbers as identity fixtures — 25 of the 29 in use were
431	# live issues or PRs, and #42 is still OPEN. A run keyed to one of those writes
432	# fabricated prior work onto that issue's state branch; measured on this repo,
433	# zbuild/state/issue-999 held 68 commits of test payloads and issue-698 held 121.
434	# Now that CI chains and pushes (#1970, #2006), that reaches origin.
435	#
436	# 9_0000000+ is unreachable: this repo is ~2000 issues in. A stray
437	# zbuild/state/issue-9xxxxxxx ref is therefore unmistakably test residue, safe to
438	# reclaim, and can never be confused with someone's work.
439	# The floor of the reserved range. Read by lint-test-identity and the hygiene
440	# test; zb_test_issue composes its ids to always land at or above it.
441	ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR=90000000
442	export ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR
443	
444	# Sequential within a test file: 90000001, 90000002, … Files repeat the same ids,
445	# which is safe because each runs in its own throwaway repo — and if one ever
446	# escapes, the number identifies it instantly.
447	# The counter lives in a FILE, not a shell variable: callers use $(zb_test_issue),
448	# which runs in a subshell, so an in-memory counter would never advance and every
449	# call would return the same id.
450	#
451	# The id is keyed on the PID so two test files running in PARALLEL never mint the
452	# same one. They otherwise all start at 90000001, and the teardown below deletes
453	# refs from the SHARED checkout — so one file's cleanup could delete a ref another
454	# file was still asserting on. The unit tier is parallel by default (#984), and
455	# more cores make that likelier, which is why it showed on Linux CI first.
456	#
457	# Shape: 9 + PID%1000 (3) + seq (4) — always 8 digits, always >= 90000000.
458	zb_test_issue() {
459	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
460	    local f="$dir/.zb-test-issue-seq"
461	    local n=0
462	    [[ -r "$f" ]] && n="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
463	    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
464	    n=$(( n + 1 ))
465	    printf '%d' "$n" > "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
466	    local id
467	    id="$(printf '9%03d%04d' "$(( $$ % 1000 ))" "$n")"
468	    # Record it, so teardown removes exactly the refs THIS file minted rather
469	    # than every reserved ref it happens to find.
470	    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> "$dir/.zb-test-issue-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
471	    printf '%s' "$id"
472	}

474	# Goal fixtures get the same treatment: the marker makes zbuild/state/goal-<hash>
475	# traceable back to a test even though the hash itself is opaque.
476	#
477	# The hash is RECORDED as it is handed out, exactly as zb_test_issue records ids.
478	# Without that, goal refs had no teardown and no guard — which is precisely how
479	# the leak fixed in this branch survived a full identity sweep unnoticed. The
480	# derivation mirrors zbuild_goal_key: sha256 of the text with all whitespace
481	# stripped, truncated to 12 hex.
482	zb_test_goal() {
483	    local text; text="$(printf '[zb-test] %s' "${1:-fixture}")"
484	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
485	    local h
486	    h="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '[:space:]' | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)"
487	    printf '%s\n' "$h" >> "$dir/.zb-test-goal-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
488	    printf '%s' "$text"
489	}

509	# Reserved-range state refs in a repo (default: the real checkout). Used by both
510	# the teardown below and the suite-wide hygiene guard.
511	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # callers live in tests/, which CI's shellcheck step
512	# does not scan (it covers scripts core plugins), so the optional repo argument
513	# looks unpassed from inside this file alone.
514	zb_test_reserved_refs() {
515	    local repo="${1:-${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}}"
516	    # Prefix glob, then a NUMERIC filter — not 'issue-9???????'. That counted
517	    # characters, so it covered 90000000-99999999 only, while lint-test-identity
518	    # and _cleanup_issue_ref_decision both gate on >= 90000000. An id above the
519	    # 8-digit range would have passed both and been invisible here.
520	    local _ref _n
521	    while IFS= read -r _ref; do
522	        [[ -n "$_ref" ]] || continue
523	        _n="${_ref##*/issue-}"
524	        [[ "$_n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
525	        # An explicit if, not `[[ … ]] && printf`: the && form returns non-zero
526	        # when the test is false, and as the last command in the loop body that
527	        # aborts callers running under `set -e`.
528	        if [[ "$_n" -ge "${ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR:-90000000}" ]]; then
529	            printf '%s\n' "$_ref"
530	        fi
531	    done < <(git -C "$repo" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' \
532	        'refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-9*' 2>/dev/null || true)
533	}

538	    # in parallel, so deleting another file's in-flight ref would fail its
539	    # assertions. Reserved-range by construction, so a real issue's branch is
540	    # never touched — not even one already contaminated.

621	# Install an envelope-aware mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
622	# Branches on argv: when invoked with `--output-format json` (ADR-018 Pattern 1
623	# decision #8, #476), wraps the payload in a {type:result,result:...} envelope
624	# so the router's `.result` extraction finds it. Otherwise emits the payload
625	# as raw text (legacy text-mode callers).
626	#
627	# Usage:
628	#   install_envelope_mock_claude <payload>                        # payload is inline text
629	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --file <payload_file>            # payload comes from a file at call time
630	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-argv <path> <payload>   # also record argv to <path>
631	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-prompt <path> <payload> # also record `-p <prompt>` to <path>
632	#
633	# Flags may be combined (e.g. --file + --record-argv).
634	install_envelope_mock_claude() {
635	    local payload="" payload_file="" argv_record="" prompt_record=""
636	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
637	        case "$1" in
638	            --file)          payload_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
639	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
640	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
641	            *)               payload="$1"; shift ;;
642	        esac
643	    done
644	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
645	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
646	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
647	#!/usr/bin/env bash
648	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude (#476).
649	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
650	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
651	fi
652	envelope_mode=0
653	prompt_text=""
654	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
655	    case "\$1" in
656	        --output-format|json) envelope_mode=1; shift ;;
657	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
658	        *)  shift ;;
659	    esac
660	done
661	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
662	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
663	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
664	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
665	fi
666	if [[ -n "${payload_file:-}" ]]; then
667	    payload="\$(cat "$payload_file")"
668	else
669	    payload=$(printf '%q' "$payload")
670	fi
671	if [[ \$envelope_mode -eq 1 ]]; then
672	    jq -n --arg r "\$payload" '{type:"result",subtype:"success",result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
673	else
674	    printf '%s\n' "\$payload"
675	fi
676	exit 0
677	MOCK
678	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
679	}

681	# Install an envelope-aware ERROR mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
682	# Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude but simulates a failed `claude` run that
683	# still prints a JSON result envelope to stdout and exits non-zero — the exact
684	# shape route.sh persists to its diagnostic sidecar
685	# (${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-…/artifacts}/stage-io/<stage>-sync-error.raw-claude-output.json).
686	#
687	# The default envelope simulates the #1052 dogfood failure: the planner burned
688	# all its turns exploring the repo and hit max_turns before emitting plan.json:
689	#   {"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","is_error":true,
690	#    "num_turns":<N>,"result":"<partial reasoning text>",
691	#    "usage":{input_tokens:…,output_tokens:…}}
692	# then `exit 1`.
693	#
694	# Everything is tunable via env vars read AT MOCK-INVOCATION TIME (not install
695	# time), so a test can export a different value just before calling plan_run and
696	# the same installed binary honors it. This lets one installer cover three cases:
697	#   (a) max_turns exhaustion (defaults).
698	#   (b) a non-max_turns crash — set ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE to e.g. "error" and the
699	#       discriminator (subtype != error_max_turns) stays on the
700	#       claude_cli_failed path.
701	#   (c) a max_turns envelope whose .result IS a valid plan.json — set
702	#       ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT to the plan JSON; recovery should salvage it.
703	#
704	# Env vars (all optional):
705	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE    envelope .subtype     (default: error_max_turns)
706	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS  envelope .num_turns   (default: 25)
707	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT     envelope .result      (default: a partial-reasoning blurb)
708	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RC         process exit code     (default: 1)
709	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR   envelope .is_error    (default: true)
710	#
711	# Usage:
712	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error                       # max_turns defaults
713	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-argv <path>  # also record argv
714	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-prompt <path> # also record -p prompt
715	#
716	# Flags may be combined. Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude's recording hooks
717	# so resume/dogfood tests can assert the captured prompt across runs.
718	install_envelope_mock_claude_error() {
719	    local argv_record="" prompt_record=""
720	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
721	        case "$1" in
722	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
723	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
724	            *)               shift ;;
725	        esac
726	    done
727	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
728	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
729	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
730	#!/usr/bin/env bash
731	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude_error (#1052).
732	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
733	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
734	fi
735	prompt_text=""
736	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
737	    case "\$1" in
738	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
739	        *)  shift ;;
740	    esac
741	done
742	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
743	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
744	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
745	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
746	fi
747	# Tunable envelope fields — read at invocation time so a test can vary the
748	# shape per call without reinstalling the mock.
749	_subtype="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE:-error_max_turns}"
750	_num_turns="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS:-25}"
751	_is_error="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR:-true}"
752	_rc="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RC:-1}"
753	_result="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT:-Explored core/ and plugins/ but ran out of turns before emitting a complete plan. Partial findings: the change touches the router and the plan plugin.}"
754	jq -n \\
755	    --arg st "\$_subtype" \\
756	    --argjson nt "\$_num_turns" \\
757	    --argjson ie "\$_is_error" \\
758	    --arg r "\$_result" \\
759	    '{type:"result",subtype:\$st,is_error:\$ie,num_turns:\$nt,result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
760	exit "\$_rc"
761	MOCK
762	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
763	}

767	# Fail loudly on an unknown platform argument. A typo (e.g. `lniux`) must NOT
768	# silently skip a test forever while still reporting success — that would let CI
769	# mask a test that never runs. Exits non-zero so the mistake surfaces.
770	_require_known_platform() {

772	        linux|macos) return 0 ;;

782	    _require_known_platform "$required"
783	    local current

785	    case "$current" in
786	        Darwin) current="macos" ;;
787	        Linux)  current="linux" ;;
788	    esac
789	    [[ "$current" == "$required" ]] && return 0
790	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
791	    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: requires '$required', running on '$current'" >&2

803	    esac
804	    [[ "$current" != "$excluded" ]] && return 0
805	    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))

912	# Creates a minimal valid stage plugin directory under $TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/.

916	# declares result_contract 3 and a JSON primary, and writes its result with the
917	# engine's writer (stage_result_write) before returning <exit_code>: `pass` on 0,

923	    local dir="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/$kind/$id"

939	    printf 'provides:\n  result_contract: 3\n' >> "$dir/manifest.yaml"
940	    [[ -n "$role" ]] && printf '  role: %s\n' "$role" >> "$dir/manifest.yaml"
941	    cat >> "$dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
942	outputs:
943	  - id: ${id//-/_}_result

945	    type: ${id}-result.json@1
946	    format: json

965	# ── zb_engine_loop_state ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
966	# Writes one loop's record into a pipeline-state.json with the ENGINE's own
967	# writers (_cycle_state_init / _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic,
968	# core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh): <rounds> rounds, then <final status>.
969	# #1799: a hand-written `cycle_iterations` holds whatever its author assumed —
970	# a field the engine never writes passed a test that wrote it itself.
971	# scripts/lib/lint-test-engine-state.sh refuses a hand-written one.
972	#
973	# Usage: zb_engine_loop_state <state_file> <loop id> <rounds> <limit> <final status>
974	zb_engine_loop_state() {
975	    local sf="$1" id="$2" rounds="$3" limit="$4" final="$5" root
976	    root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
977	    ( source "$root/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
978	      _cycle_state_init "$sf" "$id" "$(dirname "$sf")/$id-history.jsonl" "$limit" || exit 1
979	      local n
980	      for (( n = 1; n <= rounds; n++ )); do
981	          _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic "$sf" "$id" "$n" fail failed 1 in_progress || exit 1
982	      done
983	      _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic "$sf" "$id" "$rounds" fail failed 1 "$final" )
984	}

986	# ── mock_result_line ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
987	# Prints one shell line that writes the result mock_plugin_factory's manifest
988	# declares (`${artifact_dir}/<id>-result.json`), with the engine's own writer
989	# (stage_result_write, contract 3). For a test that replaces the factory's
990	# plugin.sh with its own body: embed `$(mock_result_line <id>)` in the unquoted
991	# heredoc, or the stage exits 0 with no readable result — which #1850 makes a

1053	# ─── zb_test_kill_tree <pid> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
1054	# KILL <pid> and every process under it. KILL cannot be caught, so a runner
1055	# killed alone cleans up nothing: its forked stage and the stage's time-limit
1056	# watchdog (copies of its shell, so they show as runner.sh) ran on, the watchdog
1057	# for up to the stage's limit.
1058	#
1059	# Deepest first, so no parent dies before its children (a child whose parent is
1060	# gone is re-parented away and can no longer be found), and read again until
1061	# nothing is left, for a child forked while the tree was being read. Nothing is
1062	# STOPped on the way: a stopped process whose parent dies leaves an orphaned
1063	# process group with a stopped member, and the kernel hangs up that whole group
1064	# — on macOS CI, the test's own. A process already gone is no error, under
1065	# set -e too: an abort test's runner has usually exited on its TERM by then.
1066	_zb_test_tree() { local c; printf '%s\n' "$1"; for c in $(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null || true); do _zb_test_tree "$c"; done; }
1067	zb_test_kill_tree() {
1068	    local -a t
1069	    local i r
1070	    for (( r = 0; r < 5; r++ )); do
1071	        mapfile -t t < <(_zb_test_tree "$1")
1072	        for (( i = ${#t[@]} - 1; i >= 0; i-- )); do kill -KILL "${t[i]}" 2>/dev/null || true; done
1073	        kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null || (( ${#t[@]} > 1 )) || break
1074	    done
1075	    return 0
1076	}

1078	# Bounded poll for a grep pattern to appear in an events/state file (#619's
1079	# "wait-for-event-content" pattern; reused by #887/#1127/#1149). Replaces the
1080	# anti-pattern of a fixed `sleep N` followed by a single-shot read of an
1081	# event/state file — that races a slow CI box (the writer may not have flushed
1082	# the line yet). This polls the file until the content appears, bounded by a
1083	# generous timeout so a genuinely-never-emitted event still fails fast-enough
1084	# instead of hanging.
1085	#
1086	# Usage: wait_for_event <file> <grep_pattern> [max_iters=600] [interval=0.1]
1087	#   - <grep_pattern> is a basic-regex passed to `grep -q` (quote JSON fragments,
1088	#     e.g. '"pipeline.start"').
1089	#   - Default bound: 600 × 0.1s = 60s — generous enough for a loaded shared CI
1090	#     runner, short enough to never wedge the suite.
1091	# Returns 0 as soon as the pattern is present; 1 if the bound elapses first.
1092	# Does NOT assert — callers decide whether a timeout is fatal so the failure
1093	# message stays test-specific.
1094	wait_for_event() {
1095	    local file="$1" pattern="$2" max_iters="${3:-600}" interval="${4:-0.1}" i
1096	    for (( i = 0; i < max_iters; i++ )); do
1097	        if [[ -f "$file" ]] && grep -q "$pattern" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
1098	            return 0
1099	        fi
1100	        sleep "$interval"
1101	    done
1102	    return 1
1103	}

1129	# Creates a real, minimal git repo under $TEST_TEMP_DIR/<name> with one
1130	# initial commit. Returns its absolute path on stdout. Used by integration
1131	# tests that exercise real `git checkout`/`git symbolic-ref` against an
1132	# isolated repo (issue #484).

1135	#   repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo myrepo)"

1142	        # #2103 / ADR-024: the cd MUST be fatal. `set -e` is inert inside this
1143	        # subshell because its status is tested by `|| return 1` below, so a
1144	        # failed cd would otherwise run every git command in the CALLER'S

1152	        # well-known absolute locations.

1154	            for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
1155	                [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
1156	            done
1157	        fi
1158	        [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && return 1
1159	        "$real_git" init -q -b main 2>/dev/null || "$real_git" init -q
1160	        "$real_git" config user.email "test@zbuild.local"
1161	        "$real_git" config user.name "zbuild-test"
1162	        "$real_git" config commit.gpgsign false
1163	        echo "seed" > seed.txt
1164	        "$real_git" add seed.txt
1165	        "$real_git" commit -q -m "seed"

1167	        local cur
1168	        cur="$("$real_git" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"

1177	# A bare origin whose default branch is `master` (not `main`), seeded with one
1178	# commit, plus a working clone of it whose origin/HEAD → origin/master. Prints
1179	# the clone's path; prints nothing and returns 1 on any setup failure. Extracted
1180	# from tests/integration/intake-branch-ahead-count-test.sh, where a failed seed
1181	# clone let the seeding subshell run — and `git push origin HEAD:master` — in
1182	# the caller's checkout against the caller's origin. Every cd here is fatal
1183	# because each subshell's status is tested (see setup_git_temp_repo).
1184	#
1185	# Usage:
1186	#   clone="$(setup_git_master_origin a)" || fail "setup"
1187	setup_git_master_origin() {
1188	    local label="${1:-m}"
1189	    local bare="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bare-${label}.git"
1190	    local work="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/work-${label}"
1191	    local tmp_init="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/init-${label}"
1192	
1193	    git init --bare "$bare" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1194	    git -C "$bare" symbolic-ref HEAD "refs/heads/master" 2>/dev/null || { printf ''; return 1; }
1195	
1196	    # Seed via a throwaway clone. The clone's OWN rc is checked before the
1197	    # subshell so a clone failure never reaches the cd; the cd is fatal anyway.
1198	    git clone "$bare" "$tmp_init" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1199	    (
1200	        cd "$tmp_init" || exit 1
1201	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1202	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1203	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1204	        # Unborn HEAD: -b names the branch regardless of init.defaultBranch.
1205	        git checkout -q -b master 2>/dev/null || git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/master || exit 1
1206	        echo "seed" > seed.txt || exit 1
1207	        git add seed.txt || exit 1
1208	        git commit -q -m "seed" || exit 1
1209	        git push -q origin HEAD:"refs/heads/master" || exit 1
1210	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1211	    rm -rf "$tmp_init"
1212	
1213	    # The bare repo MUST now carry master; a bare `.git` check downstream cannot
1214	    # tell "seeded" from "empty", and an unborn HEAD makes `checkout master` a no-op.
1215	    git -C "$bare" show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/master || { printf ''; return 1; }
1216	
1217	    git clone "$bare" "$work" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1218	    (
1219	        cd "$work" || exit 1
1220	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1221	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1222	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1223	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1224	
1225	    printf '%s\n' "$work"
1226	}

1228	# ── install_template_overlay (#1270) ─────────────────────────────────────────
1229	# Copy one or more template fixtures into a repo's per-repo override dir
1230	# (<repo>/.zbuild/templates/<id>.yaml), the generic ADR-016 overlay seam. A test
1231	# that then runs the engine with CWD = <repo> resolves the fixture WITHOUT any
1232	# env var and WITHOUT writing into the tracked config/templates/ — the overlay
1233	# lives entirely inside the test's temp repo (reaped by the master EXIT/INT/TERM
1234	# trap). This replaces the #1268 ZBUILD_TEMPLATES_DIR seam (reverted in #1270):
1235	# no ambient env, no global state; hermeticity comes from CWD isolation.
1236	#
1237	# Each fixture is a `.zbuild/templates/` overlay, so it MUST carry `extends: <id>`
1238	# (ADR-016). The shipped base it extends (usually `simple`) is read from the
1239	# engine tree unchanged — only the overlay id needs a fixture.
1240	#
1241	# Usage: install_template_overlay <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
1242	# install_simple_loop_continue <repo> — overlay template `simple-loop-continue`:
1243	# the shipped simple.yaml with delivery_loop set to on_max: continue.
1244	# #2241: simple.yaml's outer loop is on_max: halt, and the runner honours it.
1245	# Tests whose subject is the CONTINUE path past an exhausted loop (#766, #1217)
1246	# drive this instead — generated from the real template at test time, so it
1247	# never drifts from it. (#2369: the design loop it once also changed is retired.)
1248	install_simple_loop_continue() {
1249	    local _repo="${1:?install_simple_loop_continue: <repo> required}" _src_root
1250	    _src_root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
1251	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1252	    awk '
1253	        /^id: simple$/ { print "id: simple-loop-continue"; print "extends: simple"; next }
1254	        /^delivery_loop:/ { in_dl = 1; print; next }
1255	        in_dl && /^[a-z_-]+:/ { in_dl = 0 }
1256	        in_dl && /^  on_max: halt$/ { print "  on_max: continue"; next }
1257	        { print }
1258	    ' "$_src_root/config/templates/simple.yaml" > "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml"
1259	    grep -q '^id: simple-loop-continue$' "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml" || return 1
1260	    # Committed, as install_template_overlay_committed does: an untracked
1261	    # overlay leaves the tree dirty and intake refuses to start on it.
1262	    local _git; _git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
1263	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1264	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1265	}

1414	        key="$(zbuild_run_key "$issue" "$goal" 2>/dev/null || true)"
1415	        zbuild_layout_run_state_dir "$key" "$rid"
1416	    )
1417	}

1419	# zb_test_issue_output <dir> <issue text> — the issue as intake hands it on: a
1420	# result carrying data.issue_text (#2364), written with the engine's result
1421	# writer, so a stage finds it by what it is. Prints the file's path.
1422	zb_test_issue_output() {
1423	    local dir="$1" text="$2"
1424	    mkdir -p "$dir"
1425	    declare -F stage_result_write >/dev/null 2>&1 \
1426	        || source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/stage-result.sh"
1427	    stage_result_write "$dir/intake-result.json" pass "took in the goal" \
1428	        "$(jq -nc --arg t "$text" '{goal_len: ($t | length), platform_count: 1, issue_text: $t}')" >/dev/null
1429	    printf '%s\n' "$dir/intake-result.json"
1430	}

1432	# zb_test_deploy_output <dir> <outcome> <reason> [pr_url] [tag] [deployed] — a
1433	# deploy result written by deploy's own writer (_deploy_write_result), in a
1434	# subshell so the plugin's definitions stay out of the caller. Prints its path.
1435	zb_test_deploy_output() {

1439	        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)/plugins/agent/deploy/plugin.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1

1441	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -s "$dir/deploy-result.json" ]] \

1447	# result written by the test stage's own writer (_test_write_result), in a
1448	# subshell. Prints its path.
